text: Documentation that actually gets used — why most of it rots, and what actually prevents that.
A runbook is a specific, step-by-step response to a specific alert — what to do right now, at 2am. It survives because it gets opened during a real incident, and its gaps get fixed immediately.
A wiki page lives apart from the code and rots. A README in the same folder as an eventstream gets updated in the same pull request as a change to it — impossible to miss during review.

Proximity or enforcement, not good intentions. A runbook survives because it's read. A README survives because it's reviewed alongside the change. A data contract survives because CI checks it automatically.
Documentation that's forced to stay current, one way or another. Next up: on-call for data engineers — where a runbook actually gets used.
